title: Fix: Count Within a Limit
summary: A count of values at or below a limit is sometimes one short. Reproduce it, find the off-by-one and fix it.
statement:
`countAtMost(nums, limit)` should return how many values in `nums` are less than or equal to `limit`.

Users report that the count is sometimes one short, but not always. Use the public cases to reproduce it, find the cause and fix it. Any correct fix is accepted.
hints: Compare the failing public case with the passing ones. Where in the array is the value that wasn't counted?
Which indexes does the loop visit for an array of length 3? Write them down.
The loop stops one index early. Visit every index, `i < nums.length`, or loop over the values directly.

lab.intended_behavior: Count every value that is less than or equal to the limit, including the last one.

defect.summary: The loop condition `i < nums.length - 1` skips the last element (an off-by-one).
defect.explanation: For an array of length n the valid indexes are 0 to n - 1, so the loop should run while `i < nums.length`. With `nums.length - 1` it stops before the last index and never looks at the last value. When that value is at or below the limit, the count comes out one short.
defect.why_missed: If the last value is above the limit, skipping it changes nothing, so cases like [1, 5, 9] with limit 4 still pass. The bug only shows when the last value should have been counted.

lab.follow_up: For any loop bound, write out the indexes it visits for a length-1 and a length-3 array, and test a case where the answer depends on the last element.
lab.review_status: Authored for CodeCoach and machine-checked (the starter fails exactly its reproduction cases; the repair and an alternative pass every test). Not yet reviewed by an outside instructor.
